page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs of the arm64 AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It integrates 1900 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. The instance contains no GPUs.

Benchmark results show notable multi-core and memory throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core testing (21404.0) and PassMark memory performance (3321.52), complemented by uncached large-block memory write speeds of 182.89 GB/sec. Database performance is similarly elevated, reaching top-tier PassMark database operations scores (47242.75) and strong Redis SET throughput (67.21 million operations per second). In software compilation and static web serving, the architecture scores within the top 25%. However, large-model CPU inference shows lower throughput, with 70B parameter prompt processing falling into the bottom 25%.

The 1:1 physical-core-to-vCPU allocation ensures dedicated processing without simultaneous multithreading contention. By combining balanced ARMv9 execution efficiency with integrated high-capacity NVMe storage, m8gd.8xlarge presents a cost-effective operational profile for I/O-heavy distributed applications. It is well-suited for transactional databases, caching layers, software build clusters, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by 32 dedicated physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 128 GB of RAM, 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 15 Gbps baseline networking, with no discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-core compute capability and memory bandwidth, alongside elevated database and in-memory caching performance. Conversely, CPU-driven large language model inference shows diminished throughput on 70B parameter models. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration and dedicated local solid-state storage, m8gd.8xlarge offers strong qualitative resource density and execution efficiency for transactional databases, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized web infrastructure.
